theorem_title: Coordinate decoding of an ordered global output record
theorem_formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.OutputDecodeRecords.global_record_block {h J k : ℕ} (hk : k < _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.OutputDecodeRecords.localCount h^J) (j : Fin J) :
    ((_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.GlobalKeyEnumeration.globalRecords h J).getD k (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.OutputDecodeRecords.outputDefault h J)) j =
      (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.GlobalKeyEnumeration.localRecords h).getD (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.OutputDecodeRecords.localIndex h J k j.val) (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.OutputDecodeRecords.blockDefault h) := by sorry
theorem_natural_language_statement:
Let $h,J,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k<N(h)^J$, where $N(h)$ is the local-record count, and let $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(J)$. Coordinate $j$ of global record $k$ is exactly local record

$$\operatorname{localIndex}(h,J,k,j).$$

Both lists are read with the designated defaults; the valid-index hypothesis makes the identity agree with the ordered finite product enumeration.

This links the physical right-key index to every original block record, including duplicate key values.
